editorial:
Ever notice how a single number can start to follow you everywhere? In this dark thriller, animal control officer Walter Sparrow gets a mysterious book as a gift and quickly realizes the story inside mirrors his own life. As he digs deeper, the number 23 starts popping up in dates, addresses, and random moments, slowly pulling him into a dangerous obsession. Jim Carrey steps away from comedy here, playing a man losing his grip on reality with surprising intensity. The movie has a moody, shadowy vibe that keeps you guessing whether Walter is cursed, crazy, or something far worse. It is the kind of film that makes you look twice at license plates and phone numbers long after the credits roll.

The standout here is Carrey's committed performance, which carries the whole movie even when the plot gets a little messy. The pacing moves quickly and the visuals lean into dark, stylish territory that fits the paranoid tone. On the downside, some twists feel forced and the story can be confusing if you are not paying close attention. Still, if you enjoy psychological thrillers that mess with your head, this one delivers plenty of chills. It is best watched on a big screen in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, or you can rent it on Apple TV and grab the 4K Blu-ray for the full experience.
endingExplained: In the final twist, Walter discovers he actually wrote the book himself years ago under a different name. His obsession with the number 23 drove him to murder a woman named Laura Tollins, and he blocked out the memory. The book was his own confession all along. Once he remembers, Walter turns himself in to the police, ending his spiral and finally facing the truth about what he did.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and twist endings.
